articles.title_orig: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
articles.title_zh: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
articles.content_orig:
Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint independently uncovered two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, software used to receive and route traffic to production applications and APIs.
NGINX is a common default for the front door of modern web architectures, where it handles HTTPS and routes incoming traffic to the right application or API. As the world's most widely used open-source web server , it powers more than 225 million websites .
Successful exploitation could let attackers take control of affected NGINX servers, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services.
The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, are both rated Critical, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. The flaws are in NGINX itself. Websites and APIs can be exposed even when their own application code is secure. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. Additional conditions are described below. CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015.
We reported our findings to F5, the company behind NGINX, and collaborated with its security team on remediation and coordinated disclosure. Organizations should identify affected deployments and apply the security updates when released.
We recommend updating affected NGINX deployments to the latest release which includes multiple security fixes.
October 21, 2026: Wiz reports the HTTP/2 use-after-free vulnerability, later assigned CVE-2026-123633, to F5, including confirmed remote code execution with an ASLR bypass and a proposed fix. F5 confirms that another research team had previously reported the same vulnerability.
November 10, 2026: F5 supplies a patch for CVE-2026-123633 for review.
November 16, 2026 : Wiz reports the second HTTP/2 vulnerability, later assigned CVE-2026-123007, to F5.
November 17, 2026 : F5 confirms that the second report matches CVE-2026-123007 and is included in the planned November 18 security release.
November 18, 2026: F5 security release and coordinated public disclosure.
Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint independently uncovered  CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, two critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and reported them to F5, the company behind NGINX. Successful exploitation can compromise the server running NGINX, allowing attackers to execute code, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services.
NGINX often handles traffic for several applications, so a single affected deployment can put multiple services at risk. The flaws are in NGINX itself and can affect websites even when their own application code is secure. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. Our testing of CVE-2026-123007 demonstrated code execution on NGINX serving ordinary static files, without a backend application or third-party modules. Wiz Research used Wiz Atlas , the harness powering Wiz’s AI Code scanning solution , to discover both vulnerabilities. Our researchers used Gemini 4 Carbon and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol to validate the impact of both vulnerabilities, confirming that each could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on the server. We reported our findings to F5 and worked with its security team on remediation and coordinated disclosure. The integer underflow vulnerability dates back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015, meaning it had been hiding in the code for more than a decade. The use-after-free vulnerability had been there for nearly six years. Like the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities we reported last month and Java4Shell , disclosed yesterday by Calif, these are memory-safety flaws that have historically been extremely difficult to discover and exploit. Finding them often requires tracing subtle interactions between memory operations and multiple code paths. For years, that complexity itself created a practical barrier. AI is fundamentally dissolving that barrier. As AI models get better at following those interactions, both researchers and attackers can uncover longstanding flaws in software that powers the internet and modern applications. The fact that multiple independent research teams uncovered the same vulnerabilities in both PHP and NGINX, after they had remained in the code for years, makes this shift particularly striking. And as AI capabilities advance, each new generation of models may uncover even more complex vulnerabilities that were previously beyond practical reach. Complexity can no longer be relied upon as a barrier to discovery or exploitation. This changes not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.
Over time, finding and fixing these flaws can harden the software we all depend on. In the near term, faster discovery and a shorter window between disclosure and exploitation add to an already demanding workload for security teams. Turning a published fix into protection in production still takes substantial manual work, from validating patches to coordinating rollouts with service owners. We recommend focusing on how quickly you can reduce exposure in production. Identify deployments running the affected version and configuration, prioritize those an attacker can reach, and apply mitigations while patches are tested and rolled out. In this post, we explain the vulnerabilities and their impact, and provide mitigation and detection guidance. Organizations should identify affected deployments and apply the security updates as soon as they are available. If upgrading is not immediately possible, temporarily disable HTTP/2.
NGINX is the world's most widely used open-source web server , powering more than 225 million websites . It is commonly used as a reverse proxy in front of websites and APIs. In this role, NGINX accepts incoming requests, forwards them to the appropriate application server based on its configuration, and returns the response to the user.
NGINX can also serve web content directly and act as a load balancer , distributing traffic across multiple servers. A single NGINX deployment can serve several applications, making it a shared entry point for the websites and APIs behind it.
Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic. In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. In CVE-2026-123007, incorrect flow-control accounting leads to an invalid memory copy. Each can lead to unauthenticated remote code execution on the NGINX server.
Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled, but their additional requirements differ. CVE-2026-123633 affects reverse-proxy processing when available connection slots run low. CVE-2026-123007 can also affect NGINX serving content directly, as demonstrated in our testing over HTTPS on 64-bit systems. Typical memory safety mitigations such as ASLR do not protect against these issues, as attackers can use either vulnerabilities for memory read access prior to code execution.
On affected NGINX versions with HTTP/2 enabled, these vulnerabilities can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
The flaws are in NGINX itself. Exploitation does not depend on a bug in the website or API behind it, so applications with secure code can still be exposed. For CVE-2026-123007, we demonstrated remote code execution on a server serving ordinary static files, without a backend application or third-party module.
An attacker could use this access to run commands, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services. Because one NGINX deployment can serve several applications, the impact could extend across multiple websites and APIs.
We reported both vulnerabilities to F5 and collaborated with its security team on remediation and coordinated disclosure. We also shared proposed fixes. Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint also independently discovered and report

articles.title_orig: Brookings’ Michael O’Hanlon on China trip: I hope Trump holds the line on chips
articles.title_zh: Brookings’ Michael O’Hanlon on China trip: I hope Trump holds the line on chips
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — It took a trip to China for me, an American, to see U.S. President Donald Trump in person for the first time.
Trump emerged from a group of black-clad photographers and other personnel surrounding him at a welcome banquet in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Leaders' Meeting held November 17th to 19th.
Seated just a few spots to his left was Russian President Vladimir Putin who picked up a glass of red wine to join a toast led by Chinese President Xi Jinping .
"At tomorrow's Leaders' Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual opening up, explore pathways to innovation-driven growth, and identify opportunities to expand practical cooperation across various fields, so as to translate more initiatives into tangible results," Xi said in Mandarin, according to a CNBC translation.
Xi was speaking broadly, but Thursday's agenda includes a bilateral meeting with Trump, and their highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Putin.
But looking at the mood in the room, it seemed that their trilateral conversation had already started Wednesday night at their long banquet table. Much of what happens at APEC, including bilateral meetings and other exchanges between leaders, takes place away from the media.
But what struck me was how little sign there was of the tension surrounding Nvidia 's CEO Jensen Huang resignation, a controversy that has gripped markets for the past 10 days.
Ahead of Trump's entrance into the banquet hall, Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao shared a friendly moment with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other members of the American delegation.
Last week, the U.S. officials said that Trump did not plan to raise allegations of Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy during his meeting with Xi.
It was a striking contrast to just two months ago, when I saw photographs of Huang and Tesla CEO Elon Musk sharing a table with Trump and Xi in Washington, D.C.
And when Trump visited Beijing in May, Huang took a few minutes to speak with reporters, including me, inside the Great Hall of the People. Musk was there too, accompanied by one of his sons.
This time, neither were visible in a room that was closely watched by the world. Musk was expected to join Trump's delegation in Shenzhen, but I did not see him Wednesday evening.
Their absence from the government-heavy banquet was striking. The world's most powerful leaders may be grappling with the implications of artificial intelligence, but they certainly didn't need the industry's biggest names at the table to do so.
China's Xi calls for removing trade and investment barriers
Putin says EU is losing industry, falling behind competition
Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Over the months I've spent following APEC's "China Year," one thing has become clear: The forum has given Beijing an opportunity to host the U.S., Japan and other member economies at a time when unresolved tensions might otherwise have made such gatherings difficult.
But even in a year defined by talks of U.S.-China "strategic stability," the APEC events have exposed the rifts and the shifting dynamics in global power. Those dynamics were on display for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
Several hundred attendees, from Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun to U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, arrived early for the opening of the APEC CEO Summit.
After waiting in silence for at least 10 minutes, the audience welcomed Xi in a distinctly modern way: by raising their smartphones to capture the moment. The applause was rather muted.
It was much the same at the more government-heavy welcome banquet that evening. So many attendees rushed to take their own photographs of Xi and other leaders entering the room that reporters' views were largely blocked.
Following Xi's morning speech, there was a lengthy intermission before Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took the stage.
"The entire multilateral framework needs to change," he said, praising China on its "rare" recognition of smaller countries.
During the tea break that followed, attendees quickly resumed mingling. Some even brought coffee and snacks back into the room as Putin prepared to speak.
They listened as the Russian president talked about his country's economic resilience and claimed Europe was losing ground. As attendees headed to lunch, one thing stood out: Neither Trump nor any other G7 leader had taken the stage at the opening event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke later in the afternoon.
The most visible American presence during the morning session came from business leaders appearing in a promotional video ahead of Xi's speech.
And the absence of an American voice was perhaps even more noticeable at Wednesday evening's banquet.
Trump did not follow Xi with a toast of his own. This was the same famously outspoken president, who in a winding speech in Davos, had declared that the U.S. must get Greenland .
Yet on Wednesday night in China, Trump wasn't the one holding the microphone.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto staff 'caught red-handed' in confidentiality breach, tribunal hears
articles.content_orig:
Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100 , external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming website IGN , external branding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome," reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote , external , but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For The New York Times , external one of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, with The Guardian , external describing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes , external , Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
The Washington Post , external said GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", while Bloomberg , external 's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (Â£760m).
GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.
Additional reporting by Jasmine Sandhar

articles.title_orig: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, Farm Bureau says
articles.title_zh: Americans will pay more for Thanksgiving dinners this year, Farm Bureau says
articles.content_orig:
For the first time since 2022, American shoppers will see an increase in the price of goods for Thanksgiving dinner. Results from the American Farm Bureau Federation's 41st annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey indicate that the price of a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 people averages $58.63, up 6% from a year ago.
Over Four Decades of AFBF Thanksgiving Surveys
Each November, as millions of Americans prepare to gather with their family and friends to celebrate Thanksgiving, hundreds of volunteer shoppers from all 50 states and Puerto Rico participate in AFBF's annual Thanksgiving dinner cost survey. Every year since 1986, shoppers have reported prices for a standard list of items at their local grocery store for a variety of ingredients used to craft Thanksgiving favorites. Up until 2018, the survey included carrots, celery, cranberries, cubed stuffing, dinner rolls, frozen green peas, sweet potatoes, pumpkin pie mix, frozen pie crusts, whole milk, heavy whipping cream, and the ubiquitous American holiday staple: turkey. In 2018, AFBF added ham, frozen green beans and russet potatoes to better reflect the price of an all-American Thanksgiving meal.
While the overall cost of Thanksgiving dinner ticked upward in 2026, prices for several items included in the survey decreased slightly from 2025. A vegetable tray containing celery and carrots posted the largest percentage decline in this year's survey, with a 3.7% decrease compared to a year ago. In terms of absolute dollar changes, frozen pie crusts had the sharpest decrease, posting a decrease of 9 cents compared to a year ago. The survey bodes well for pumpkin pie enthusiasts, who will enjoy a lower overall cost for their beloved dessert despite an increase in the cost of pumpkin pie mix, as heavy whipping cream is also cheaper in 2026 compared to last year.
Higher Prices for Several Thanksgiving Favorites
The overall cost of a 10-person Thanksgiving dinner increased for 2026, largely fueled by increases in items key to the Turkey Day menu. The most notable increase for 2026 is the turkey itself, with the average price of a 16 pound frozen bird being $23.68, an increase of $2.38 (10%) from 2025. As discussed in a recent Farm Bureau Intel , strong demand and tight inventories have led to increased prices for turkey in 2026.
Apart from turkey, other widely featured Thanksgiving items increased in this year's survey. Grocery store prices for boneless ham, milk, dinner rolls, sweet potatoes, russet potatoes, frozen peas, frozen green beans, cranberries, and cubed stuffing (known in some regions as “dressing”) all increased in 2026.
Higher prices for these items aren't a complete surprise, as the effects of significant spikes in prices for critical inputs throughout the supply chain, like fuel for processing and transportation, have made their way to consumers. America's farmers and ranchers also face significant challenges, with record diesel costs, elevated fertilizer prices, increased labor expenses, and a bigger bill for items like rent and electricity — all of which hurt their ability to breakeven at the end of the year. However, unlike wholesalers and retailers, farmers aren’t able to pass those costs up the supply chain
Thanksgiving Dinner Prices Vary Across the Country
At an average of $61.57 for a 10-person classic Thanksgiving dinner, the Northeast has the highest cost. The Northeast's dinner basket cost is about 5% higher than the national average.  The average cost for a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 in the West and Midwest is closer to the national average, at $58.74 and $56.89, respectively. The South's average dinner cost is $54.33.
Some Shoppers May Find Great Deals
Despite the overall increase in the average cost of Thanksgiving dinner this year, some of our shoppers were able to find staggering deals on a variety of items, including turkey, which some shoppers reported finding  for as low as 69 cents per pound, nearly half the average nationwide price for a pound of turkey.  As Thanksgiving approaches, shoppers will look for deals on a variety of items to bring down the cost of their Thanksgiving dinner grocery list.
Higher Grocery Prices Do Not Mean Higher Farm Profits
Farm Bureau's 2026 Thanksgiving Dinner market basket survey indicates that Americans will pay more to feed family and friends this Thanksgiving. Nearly all items surveyed increased in price compared to 2025, with turkey, milk and cranberries posting some of the largest year-over-year percentage gains. However, higher grocery prices do not necessarily translate into better returns for America's farmers and ranchers.
Farmers and ranchers are largely price-takers, not price-makers, and receive only a small share of what consumers spend at the grocery store. USDA's Food Dollar Series estimates that less than 6 cents of every dollar spent on food goes back to the farm. Even when higher retail prices translate into increased farm revenue, rising production costs can quickly offset those gains. Elevated prices for critical inputs such as diesel, fertilizer and equipment continue to squeeze farm margins.
For example, this year's survey found that a 12-ounce bag of cranberries costs nearly 9% more than last year. That increase does not necessarily mean the Wisconsin cranberry farmer who grew them is receiving a higher price. Even if the farmer does capture some additional revenue, those earnings are needed to cover increased fertilizer, fuel and other production expenses.
As Americans gather around the Thanksgiving table, it's important to remember that higher food prices can place pressure on both consumers and the farmers who produce that food. Wherever and however you celebrate this Thanksgiving, take a moment to thank America's farmers and ranchers, who continue working through challenging economic conditions to provide the food, fuel and fiber we rely on every day.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang Scandal: Timeline That Led To His Resignation—And Potential Comeback
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang Scandal: Timeline That Led To His Resignation—And Potential Comeback
articles.content_orig:
Humilis Investment Strategies CEO and CIO Brian Belski joins Taylor Riggs to analyze Nvidia's third-quarter earnings beat, showing a 103% year-over-year revenue surge. They also discuss the board's decision regarding Jensen Huang.
Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman on Wednesday took aim at Nvidia’s board of directors, accusing them of "not acting in the best interest of shareholders " in the sudden ouster of CEO Jensen Huang.
In a fiery post on X, the Pershing Square Capital Management chief executive argued that the tech giant’s leadership "panicked" over negative headlines rather than conducting proper due diligence.
"What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy," Ackman wrote.
"They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders. They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts."
NVIDIA INTERIM CEO SAYS 'WE’VE GOT THIS' AS COMPANY LOOKS TO FUTURE WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG
Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman on Wednesday took aim at Nvidia’s board of directors. (John Lamparski/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
Ackman questioned how the board could have properly deliberated on a move with massive implications for shareholders and customers, pointing to the rapid timeline of Huang's exit.
"It takes time to convene a board meeting," Ackman said. "There was time, maybe, for one Zoom. And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known."
While acknowledging that corporate boards have the authority to remove a chief executive over an "inappropriate relationship with a subordinate," Ackman said it should not be an "automatic decision."
"That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents. A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders," Ackman said.
Ackman also questioned the legal counsel advising Nvidia's directors, arguing they failed to uphold their "duty of care."
"Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here," he said. "What law firm is advising this board?"
NVIDIA HALTS CHINA AI CHIP SHIPMENTS DESPITE US APPROVAL
Ackman further criticized the board for ruling out any possibility of Huang's return .
"And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO. Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known?" Ackman questioned. "This is yet another breach of their duty of care."
Ackman questioned how the board could have properly deliberated on a move with massive implications for shareholders and customers, pointing to the rapid timeline of Huang's exit. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)
He also warned that the board's internal investigation could inflict further damage on the chipmaker.
"Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope," he said.
"In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media , not because it was the right thing for them company. They couldn’t stand the heat."
NVIDIA RELEASES QUARTERLY EARNINGS, SUGGESTS FUTURE PLANS AFTER JENSEN HUANG'S RESIGNATION
Huang stepped down on Nov. 12 after an internal investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, the company announced at the time. (Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images)
Huang stepped down on Nov. 12 after an internal investigation into his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, the company announced.
CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO
The former Nvidia CEO said Tuesday he would be willing to return to lead the AI giant, but board Chairman Harvey Jones shut down the speculation on the company's earnings call, stating the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
FOX Business reached out to Nvidia for comment.

articles.title_orig: The Fed's next moves come into focus
articles.title_zh: The Fed's next moves come into focus
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Federal Reserve governor Chris Waller said Wednesday that if the central bank hikes interest rates by a quarter point next month, it will need to signal that the Fed will hike again by that much in January.
Otherwise, the Fed needs to raise rates by a jumbo half percentage point in December.
"People have argued, do you do 50 in December, nothing in January, or 25 in December, 25 in January," Waller said in an interview Wednesday on CNBC. "But when you do 25 now and you're going to do 25 in January, it only affects market pricing if you signal you're going to do it, and you give the markets a credible signal."
Waller said that if you leave the market guessing about a January rate increase, there won't be an effect on the market and, by extension, the economy.
"If you're not going to signal this very clearly to markets you're going in January, my view is then you have to go 50 in December," Waller said.
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
That sounds a lot like forward guidance, which Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has sought to eliminate since taking the reins in May. Warsh has said that telegraphing future policy moves distorts market signals and boxes in policymakers.
But Warsh's philosophy hasn't quite taken hold, as other Fed members have continued to offer clues about the path ahead — which has also led to more questions and at times confusion in markets.
Without using the term explicitly, Waller argued Wednesday that the Fed would need to use forward guidance if it doesn't deliver a jumbo hike next month. He said the central bank could signal its next move either in the statement or at Warsh's press conference. He added that quarterly interest rate projections, which will be released in December, would be helpful this time because it's the end of the year and the projections would be for all of next year.
Waller said the Fed needs to be more aggressive because inflation is moving higher after remaining above the central bank's 2% goal for nearly six years.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Waller first hinted at a jumbo hike last week, saying ahead of the Consumer Price Index release, that if inflation came in higher than expected, stronger action would be needed.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2%.
On Wednesday, Waller said the Fed needs to take back the three rate cuts from last year and may need to do more to get inflation to come back down.
New York Federal Reserve president John Williams doesn't share that view.
Asked Tuesday during a Q&A with Axios in New York whether that latest inflation data calls for a supersize rate hike soon, Williams said, "I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action."

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq rises in choppy trade as investors weigh Nvidia outlook, Anthropic IPO
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq rises in choppy trade as investors weigh Nvidia outlook, Anthropic IPO
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Nvidia ( NVDA ) interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress gets an "A" for the financial performance and a "C" for the optics displayed on Tuesday's late-evening earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones — whom most Nvidia faithful have never heard of or from — gets a "C-" for his performance on the call.
The reality is Nvidia's leadership needs a better overall grade in the months ahead to sustainably win back market support.
Nvidia just put up another monster quarter, no doubt about it. Revenue and earnings easily topped expectations. Its outlook for the current quarter came in ahead of Wall Street estimates. Management pointed to approximately 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, up from the roughly 70% growth outlook then CEO Jensen Huang had previously discussed three months ago when he led the earnings call.
Let that sink in. Nvidia is talking about growing revenue at an extraordinary rate at a scale few companies in history have ever approached. Shares are up 2.5% on Wednesday in response.
There was more. The company cited a $2.5 trillion cloud backlog, expressed confidence that its next-generation chips will be released on schedule, and signaled that aggressive share repurchases will continue.
"FY28 underwritten as concern on near-term is largely addressed," Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley said.
But then there was the earnings call itself. And this is where things went astray.
This was Colette Kress's moment. The veteran Nvidia CFO is now Nvidia's interim CEO, stepping into a role that suddenly carries enormous weight following the leadership upheaval surrounding the disgraced Jensen Huang.
Yet the call felt strangely detached from the magnitude of what is happening inside the company.
Eight analysts asked questions. Not one mentioned Jensen's name. That was in part because Nvidia stonewalled them at the start of the call by saying it wouldn't answer any Jensen questions. This was tone deaf by Jones and Kress, and the analyst community did a horrible job of adhering to such bullshit from the world's most important stock.
Kress didn't mention his name either. Not once.
I found that remarkable. This is the man who founded Nvidia in 1993, helped build the products driving today's results, and became the face of the global AI revolution. The quarter being discussed was built on years of work under his intense leadership. The products shipping over the next 18 to 24 months will largely reflect that legacy too.
You don't have to turn an earnings call into a tribute to acknowledge reality.
Jones stumbled over remarks that sounded like he was reading from a fast-moving teleprompter. Maybe he is rusty at being in the public spotlight after years of yachting and home renovation work in his town of Nantucket, as this new profile would suggest .
Jones and Kress also leaned heavily on prepared remarks when addressing employees and the leadership transition. The message was essentially that employees remain committed and the company will take care of them. Fine. But investors deserve more than carefully rehearsed reassurances at a moment like this and in the wake of once-teflon Nvidia shares being down almost 30% in a month.
There was another important clue buried in the call: Kress sounded more measured about Nvidia's financial support for the so-called neocloud companies, including CoreWeave ( CRWV ). Nvidia has been an aggressive financial backer of parts of this AI ecosystem. Kress's comments suggested a more disciplined approach could be coming.
That matters. Nvidia needs customers with real businesses, real cash flows, and the ability to pay for the enormous amounts of computing infrastructure they are buying. The AI boom cannot run forever on circular financing and promises.
So here's where I land: The stock's initial positive reaction makes sense. The numbers were powerful. The demand outlook was explosive, as Kress characterized it. Nvidia is still an extraordinary business. But the company has a leadership problem to solve that quarterly revenue and profit beats cannot fix.
"We remain Sector Weight [rated], as uncertainty regarding who Jensen's successor will be likely keeps the stock range-bound," KeyBanc analyst John Vinh said.
Kress is a capable, experienced executive. She knows the numbers better than almost anyone. Nvidia clearly needs a permanent CEO who can combine technical credibility, strategic vision, and the kind of public-facing salesmanship that made Jensen Huang such a force.
You aren't going to find another Jensen. The assignment is to convince Wall Street that Nvidia's future doesn't depend on one person.
On earnings day, the numbers said yes. The earnings call didn't quite get there.
Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show, the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title_orig: Social Security update: Medicare’s new monthly premium announced, what it means for retirees
articles.title_zh: Social Security update: Medicare’s new monthly premium announced, what it means for retirees
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Medicare surcharges hit far below the wealthy: singles earning just over $112,000 pay about $1,200 more, and a single extra dollar triggers the full increase.
Medicare prices 2027 premiums off your 2025 tax return, so a $50,000 Roth conversion can add roughly $2,400 to a couple's annual costs.
Medicare's trap hinges on taxable income, not total wealth, so calculate your projected income before large withdrawals, gains, or conversions.
Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)
Retirement is supposed to be when decades of saving finally pay off. Yet for Americans who have accumulated sizable 401(k)s, IRAs, and investment portfolios, success can bring an unexpected expense. The federal government increasingly treats retirement income differently depending on how much you receive and where it comes from. That can turn an otherwise sensible investment decision into a costly mistake.
The latest Medicare premium announcement illustrates the problem. Some retirees will pay nearly $10,000 for coverage in 2027, even before accounting for their prescription drug plan premiums, deductibles, and other out-of-pocket expenses. And the real trap isn't necessarily how much money they've saved.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced Nov. 17 that the standard Medicare Part B premium will rise to $209.40 monthly in 2027, up from $202.90 this year.
That's $2,512.80 annually. But higher-income retirees face an additional charge called the income-related monthly adjustment amount, or IRMAA.
At the highest income tier, the numbers look considerably different:
Highest Part B premium, including IRMAA
Highest Part D income surcharge
Combined Part B and D charges
The $9,698.40 figure excludes the actual Part D insurance premium, which varies by plan. Reaching that highest tier requires modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) of at least $500,000 for individuals or $750,000 for married couples filing jointly.
Many successful investors eventually reach the same moment. The saving is done, the portfolio is built, and the question quietly changes from how much can I grow this to how much can I take out? Get that second question wrong and decades of good investing can come apart in a handful of years.
That is exactly what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps answer. It covers what your retirement could actually cost, which income sources are worth using, and the withdrawal math that decides whether the money lasts. It is free today from Fisher Investments. Read More Here ›
Surprisingly, the Medicare surcharge problem begins much further down the income ladder. Single retirees earning more than $112,000, or married couples exceeding $224,000, face higher premiums. Crossing that first threshold increases annual Part B and Part D charges by $1,189.20 per person. Just $1 of additional income can trigger the entire increase.
Even a $1 mistake on your tax return can skyrocket your Medicare premiums by thousands. Learn why your hard-earned retirement savings might actually be a hidden tax trap in 2027. © 24/7 Wall St.
Here's where successful retirement planning can backfire. Medicare generally calculates 2027 premiums using income reported on your 2025 federal tax return. That two-year lookback means a financial decision made years earlier can determine what you pay today.
Consider a married couple with $200,000 in annual retirement income. They're comfortably below the $224,000 surcharge threshold.
Now suppose they convert $50,000 from a traditional IRA into a Roth IRA. Their MAGI climbs to $250,000, triggering higher Medicare premiums two years later. If both spouses have Part B and Part D coverage, that single conversion adds $2,378.40 to their annual Medicare costs under 2027 rates. The conversion also generates an immediate income-tax liability.
That's why large Roth conversions can become expensive Medicare mistakes, even when they make sense for long-term tax planning.
Other income sources can create similar problems. Required minimum distributions, realized capital gains, and even tax-exempt municipal bond interest can push retirees into higher IRMAA brackets.
The good news is that wealthy retirees have options. Qualified Roth IRA withdrawals don't increase MAGI. That makes an established Roth account valuable for generating retirement cash without raising Medicare premiums.
Investors can also spread Roth conversions across multiple years rather than recognizing one large taxable amount. Qualified charitable distributions from IRAs, available beginning at age 70-1/2, can help eligible retirees satisfy required distributions without adding that amount to adjusted gross income.
There is another potential escape hatch. The Social Security Administration allows retirees experiencing qualifying life-changing events, including retirement or a spouse's death, to request an IRMAA adjustment using Form SSA-44.
However, voluntarily selling appreciated investments or converting an IRA generally doesn't qualify for that relief.
In short, Medicare's hidden tax trap is about taxable income, not accumulated wealth. A retiree with a $3 million portfolio could pay the standard premium, while someone with considerably less might face surcharges after a poorly timed withdrawal.
The smartest move is to calculate your projected MAGI before making large withdrawals, realizing investment gains, or converting retirement accounts. Review the potential Medicare cost alongside the income-tax consequences.
After all, building a substantial retirement portfolio takes decades. Keeping more of it shouldn't come down to overlooking a $1 income threshold.

It may be the least discussed and most consequential transition in personal finance, and plenty of otherwise careful investors walk into it with no real plan. articles.title_orig: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.title_zh: UnitedHealth and other insurance stocks drag down the Dow after CMS proposes new anti-fraud rule
articles.content_orig:
Today’s big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?
UnitedHealth Group (UNH) stock fell 5.4% on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.0%. There was no announcement, earnings report or filing from the company. A market commentary published that day said the shares fell amid renewed regulatory scrutiny. All seven other managed health care companies worth $2 billion or more fell too. Management’s comments on its October earnings call, weeks before the fall, show which parts of UnitedHealth’s business sit closest to regulators.
Where Is UnitedHealth Exposed To Regulation?
By management’s own account, rules set outside the company affect both its government plans and its commercial business. On its October 13 call, management said policy-driven regulatory developments continue to reshape the industry.
In Medicaid, UnitedHealth works with states on rates that reflect the impacts of regulatory actions. Management said the timing of those updates remains uneven. The company expects 2026 to be the low point for core Medicaid margins. It expects those margins to come in moderately better than a 1% loss.
In the commercial business, management pointed to the dispute process under the No Surprises Act. It said a small number of clinician groups and third-party organizations abuse that process. Arbitration awards can reach nearly 6% of total medical spend in some regions, management said.
UnitedHealth has little room to absorb such costs . The company recorded a net margin of 3.5% over the twelve months to September 2026, down from 4.0% a year earlier.
Did UnitedHealth Fall With Other Managed Care Companies?
Yes, and it fell further than any of them. All seven other companies worth $2 billion or more in its managed health care sub-industry fell on Tuesday, logging a median drop of 3.9%. Just one of them fell 5% or more: Molina Healthcare, down 5.1%.
Every company on UnitedHealth’s peer list fell as well , among them Humana, down 3.9%. The broader health care sector fell less, with the sector fund XLV down 1.4%. UnitedHealth moved with its group, and its drop was larger than the group’s median.
Where UnitedHealth Stock Stands After The Fall
A fall this large is rare for UnitedHealth. Only one other session in the prior year brought a fall at least this big: a 19.6% drop on January 27, 2026.
Over the past twelve months, the stock returned 24.3%, against 10.3% for the S&P 500. Shares climbed from a 52-week closing low of $259.02 on March 27 to a high of $436.35 on July 21. Tuesday’s close of $389.68 left the stock below that high. UnitedHealth trades at 0.78 times its sales over the past twelve months, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500.
UnitedHealth is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in January 2027. The number to watch is the medical care ratio, the share of premiums spent on care, which the company put at 88.4% for the third quarter.
Tuesday showed how one stock can drop with its whole group on a day its company announced nothing.
Could You Hold On Through The Next Fall?
Holding on is easier when your portfolio falls less than the market. For every dollar its benchmark lost, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio lost about 81 cents on average, holding 30 quality stocks in equal weight.

articles.title_orig: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.title_zh: iPhone 20 Pro Rumored to Return to Titanium
articles.content_orig:
Apple's rumored "iPhone 20 Pro" could return to titanium as part of a more rounded design, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo , the leaker said the iPhone 20 Pro will adopt a titanium frame with a more rounded design. A frame made of titanium is reportedly currently in use on prototype devices during early engineering work. They described the design as somewhat similar to the iPhone Air , but substantially more rounded.
If the claim proves accurate, it would mark a return to titanium for the Pro lineup. Apple used titanium frames for the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 16 Pro, before switching to an aluminum unibody design with the iPhone 17 Pro in 2025. Apple highlighted aluminum's thermal conductivity as part of that redesign, which also introduced a vapor chamber to improve sustained performance.
While the change was praised for its improved thermals, light weight, and distinctive design, some users missed the more premium look and feel of titanium, along with its superior resistance to damage. The latest report regards development hardware, so it is still open whether titanium will be used in the finished product, but it seems plausible. The ‌iPhone Air‌ and iPhone Duo continue to use titanium frames.
The leaker's comparison with the ‌iPhone Air‌ builds on earlier claims about how Apple is developing the anniversary models. Earlier this week, Fixed Focus Digital said the devices would use the same glass material as the ‌iPhone Air‌, reshaped with greater curvature along all four sides.
An illustration accompanying that post depicted curved front and rear glass meeting a narrow, polished metal frame. In August, Fixed Focus Digital claimed that Apple had modified iPhone Air manufacturing equipment to produce the more rounded glass components.
That combination of curved glass and a narrow metal frame is consistent with Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman 's reporting that Apple is planning front and rear glass panels that curve into the sides around a thin metal band . Gurman said an earlier, more ambitious version that replaced even more metal with glass had been abandoned during development.
The latest claim suggests titanium could form that remaining band. Gurman described the planned changes as the biggest overhaul of the Pro line since the iPhone X.
The extent of the curvature may still be under consideration. The leaker "Ice Universe" today claimed that Apple is developing four models with two different designs , including two with flat glass and two with glass that curves along all four edges. Apple has reportedly explored the curved design for three years, reducing the more pronounced curvature of earlier versions.
The curved models are said to have borders measuring around 1mm, with the surrounding glass making them appear almost invisible when viewed head-on. Screen protector samples circulating online offer a physical illustration of that approach, showing rounded corners, shallow curves along all four edges, and very narrow borders.
Alongside the changes to the glass and frame, the displays could grow slightly. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has claimed that the Pro and Pro Max models will feature 6.41-inch and 6.96-inch screens , respectively, while also describing a four-sided curved design intended to appear borderless.
Separately, Ice Universe suggested that the main camera could gain a sensor with logic circuitry manufactured using a 17-nanometer process , potentially enabling faster readout speeds and improved power efficiency. The device could also lose the Action button and feature the "A21 Pro" chip based on TSMC's enhanced 2nm process (N2P).
Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone models are expected to launch in the fall of 2027. Leakers have referred to the devices as the "iPhone 20 Pro," but Apple's actual naming plans are unknown.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.title_zh: Nvidia's Chinese whispers reach Indian-American executive Jay Puri
articles.content_orig:
Matthew Field is a Senior Technology Reporter covering the UK tech sector. He has covered social media giants, technology policy and British start-ups for The Telegraph since 2017. He also writes about the space industry. He can be reached at matthew.field@telegraph.co.uk or via X @matthfield
The wife of one of Jensen Huang’s most senior allies has been caught up in a chip-smuggling scandal that has engulfed one of Nvidia’s biggest partners.
Cenly Chen, who is reportedly married to Jay Puri, an Nvidia executive, worked at Super Micro, a technology company where senior executives have been accused of smuggling $2.5bn (£1.9bn) worth of chips to China.
In a lawsuit brought by shareholders of Super Micro, investors allege there was “no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company’s illicit sales”. Super Micro has yet to file a response to the claims.
Ms Chen was previously chief growth officer at Super Micro, which packages Nvidia chips into computer servers.
US prosecutors charged some of the company’s leading executives earlier this year over involvement in an illicit chip smuggling scheme.
Super Micro has insisted it has co-operated with the US government’s investigation and has not been named in its indictment. Ms Chen is not named in the US charges.
However, the revelations come amid mounting scrutiny on Nvidia’s ties to the Far East over claims Mr Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Muddy waters, a short-selling firm, raised questions over Ms Chen’s ties to Nvidia on Tuesday night.
The firm noted how Ms Chen had been repeatedly photographed alongside Mr Puri and named in photographs as Cenly Puri.
The pair are reportedly married, technology news site The Information reported on Wednesday.
Nvidia has already been the subject of intense pressure over claims that Chinese companies sought to access its chips through illegal smuggling and legal loopholes.
Nvidia’s graphics chips are widely used to develop powerful AI technology.
The Super Micro scandal, which emerged earlier this year, saw Wally Liaw, the company’s co-founder, charged by the US government for allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia chips via Taiwan to customers in China.
Mr Liaw has pleaded not guilty to the charges.
Mr Huang resigned last Thursday over claims he had a relationship with Alice Huang, who worked at another Nvidia customer, Megaspeed.
Megaspeed, based in Singapore, has also been investigated by the US for smuggling over claims it diverted powerful Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.
Nvidia’s board rejected an attempt by Mr Huang to return to the company on Tuesday, insisting it had no plans to reinstate him.
The fallout has also triggered scrutiny in the White House.
It emerged on Wednesday that leading Democrats in the US House of Representatives have launched an investigation into whether Howard Lutnick, the US commerce secretary, had used his position to help Cantor Fitzgerald avoid losses from the Nvidia scandal.
Cantor Fitzgerald is controlled by Mr Lutnick’s two sons.
The letter asked questions about the firm’s trading related to Nvidia, and any “actions or decisions” by Mr Lutnick that may have been “improperly influenced” by Cantor’s business interests.
A Cantor spokesman said any suggestion its work had influenced government decisions was “baseless” and that it held “no material” shares in Nvidia.
Nvidia, Super Micro and Ms Chen were contacted for comment.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.title_zh: Nvidia retreats, weighs on AI stocks as strong outlook fails to dispel Huang uncertainty
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted former CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and does not intend to reinstate him as chief executive, board chair Harvey Jones said at the start of the company’s earnings call Tuesday night.
The announcement comes after Huang said in a statement earlier Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO, should the board allow it. Huang abruptly resigned last week amid national security concerns and reports of multiple extramarital affairs. Jones said Nvidia’s board has “every confidence” in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress to lead the company as it searches for a permanent leader.
The company sought to reassure investors and offer clarity about its future in the third-quarter earnings report Tuesday evening, with Kress, saying Nvidia’s “roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.”
“Our ambition will not change, our passion to innovate will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change,” Kress told investors, whose confidence in the company’s future has been badly shaken by the scandal , on the earnings call.
It’s the first financial picture investors are getting since the chipmaker was shaken last week by Huang’s resignation after three decades at the helm of the company he founded.
Nvidia more than doubled its quarterly revenue and profit from a year prior, and both figures beat Wall Street’s expectations.
Lies, spies and sex are just one part of the Nvidia story. The real stakes are much bigger
Nvidia’s earnings — the numbers and executives’ comments — have long been viewed as a bellwether for the larger AI industry, with Nvidia’s technology and funding at the heart of much of the boom. That’s especially true now with questions swirling about the industry’s future without Huang, its biggest cheerleader and dealmaker, at the helm.
Nvidia shares were coming off their worst week in 19 months heading into the report. The stock is down 16.7% since Huang admitted to an extramarital affair and Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, erasing $751 billion in market value. Since Nvidia shares hit their record high on October 6, they have dropped 35%, erasing roughly $2 trillion in market value.
Ahead of the report, Siebert Financial Chief Investment Officer Mark Malek wrote that it would be the “most important in the company’s history.”
Nvidia shares have dropped for four consecutive days since Huang resigned. Shares fell just 0.44% Tuesday. But shares moved higher in after-hours trading after the earnings release and analyst call, gaining roughly 5% as of 6:10 p.m. ET.
“The massive results, strong guidance and reassurance that the strategy Huang put in place remains firmly on track show that an orderly CEO transition does not necessarily have to dilute the company’s value,” Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com, said in emailed commentary following the release. He added that Nvidia’s growth train “can continue with or without Huang, provided the company makes the right call on leadership.”
Nvidia’s board said last week that Kress, the company’s CFO of 13 years, would serve as interim CEO as it considered internal and external candidates to permanently fill the role. Nvidia’s board also said Tuesday it had established a new national security and export control oversight committee to ensure the company is abiding by global trade regulations, and that it will strengthen its internal national security and compliance initiatives.
Some Nvidia employees, investors and other tech leaders had called on the board to reinstate Huang as CEO, pending the outcome of its investigation into his multiple reported extramarital affairs, including with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang , whom US officials suspect as a potential Chinese intelligence asset; and at least one direct subordinate at Nvidia.
Huang said Tuesday that he would be “honored” to return as CEO if the board decided that his “return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America,” in his first public comment since resigning.
Jones said during Tuesday’s call that he would not take additional questions regarding Huang’s resignation or the company’s investigation, but that the board would “communicate further when appropriate.” Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing, joined Kress to take analyst questions on the call — a signal of his importance as a senior leader at the company.
Meanwhile, Huang is set to testify on Capitol Hill on December 1. He is expected to face questions about his relationship with Alice Huang and Nvidia’s sales of chips to Singapore-based Megaspeed, which some US officials believed should have been labeled a national security risk.
Some US sources say that whether or not Alice Huang was recruited by China’s intelligence service, she posed a counterintelligence risk because Chinese national security law requires its citizens to assist in intelligence-gathering efforts if asked. Concerns have been mounting that chips Megaspeed purchased were diverted to Chinese entities, potentially skirting US export restrictions.
Huang’s exit aside, concerns about whether the AI trade is a bubble about to burst, with valuations and infrastructure spending outpacing returns, had already begun to reach a fever pitch in recent months. Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN this week that he believes the AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election.
Nvidia’s Tuesday report indicates that, at least for now, the company’s growth continues to outpace Wall Street’s expectations.
The company posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, up 103% year-on-year. Profits reached more than $65 billion, up 105% year-on-year. Kress also said demand for the company’s next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology is “off to an explosive start,” with the tech already in use by customers such as Google, Microsoft and Oracle.
Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains strong, with a handful of the biggest AI and cloud companies expected to shell out more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures next year alone. But in the wake of Huang’s exit, investors have been more concerned with the company’s future business.
The report also comes after a blue wave in the US midterm elections ushered in a slate of newly elected leaders, many of whom campaigned on slowing or restricting data center development, which could dent Nvidia’s business.
Analysts with research firm IDC wrote in a report last week that the firm sees “near-term AI infrastructure demand and supply as largely locked in, so the harder questions,” like long-term bets on emerging technologies and the financing system that Jensen Huang sat in the center of , “sit further out.”
Nvidia said it expects fourth-quarter revenue to come in around $130 billion, plus or minus 3% — exceeding what Wall Street analysts had predicted, according to consensus estimates from FactSet.
Kress raised the company’s growth estimates for next year even higher from its already-ambitious targets, saying Nvidia’s revenue is expected to grow by 75% in fiscal 2028, up from 70% in the last earnings call.
Significant questions also remain about the future of Nvidia’s business in China, and potentially in Asia more broadly, as US officials react to the national security concerns surrounding the company.
Shipments of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China made up less than 1% of sales in its core data center business in the previous quarter . However, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., estimated that China and Hong Kong “could comprise roughly 15% of revenues when considering potential loopholes throughout Asia.”

articles.title_orig: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.title_zh: Trump Says the U.S. Will “Catch” China on Rare Earths Within 10 Months - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — In a rare and surprising move, Chinese leader Xi Jinping personally greeted President Donald Trump as he arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of historic three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
It is believed to be the first time that Xi, in power for more than a decade, has been on hand to greet any foreign leader arriving in China.
He was reciprocating the personal greeting he had received from Trump in September, when the American leader met him at the plane upon his arrival for a White House state visit . Lawmakers from both parties had criticized Trump over the move, which is also rare for U.S. presidents.
A report by Xinhua, China’s state-run news agency, said that during Trump’s arrival in the city of Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi noted the special trip the American president and first lady Melania Trump had made to welcome him at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington.
“China is a nation that values courtesy and has a tradition of returning goodwill with goodwill,” the Xinhua report said.
After Trump descended from Air Force One, a handshake between the two leaders turned into a quick hug as rows of military regiments and performers wearing bright pink and turquoise outfits stood at attention. A martial band played the American and Chinese national anthems as dancers waved flowers, pompoms and Chinese and American flags.
Xi’s gesture Wednesday most likely reflects a desire by him and his government to “show respect to Trump,” which they know he enjoys, William Yang, a senior analyst for Northeast Asia at the International Crisis Group, said in a post on X .
“It is likely also an attempt to uphold the positive rapport between Xi and Trump ahead of a potentially turbulent period in U.S.-China relations in the coming months,” he said.
When Trump last visited China in May, he was greeted at the airport in Beijing by Vice President Han Zheng.
Putin, who has a close relationship with Xi and has met with him 50 times as of Wednesday, did not receive a personal greeting from the Chinese leader when he arrived earlier at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport. Putin was instead met by Cai Qi, a close Xi adviser and member of the Politburo Standing Committee.
Xi has met with a number of world leaders, including Putin, as they gather in Shenzhen this week for a summit of Asia-Pacific economies.
Trump, Putin and Xi are holding an unprecedented trilateral meeting Thursday on the sidelines of the summit.
Ahead of his bilateral meeting with Xi on Wednesday, Putin said he expected “great potential benefits” from the trilateral talks, which have sparked anxiety in places such as Ukraine, Iran and the Beijing-claimed island of Taiwan, where officials worry the world’s three most powerful leaders could make decisions about their futures without consulting them.
In a briefing last week, a senior U.S. official said the trilateral meeting was unlikely to produce any sort of agreement, describing it as an “entry point” and “the first conversation.”
Jennifer Jett is the Asia Digital Editor for NBC News, based in Hong Kong.
Erin Tan is a news researcher in NBC News’s Beijing bureau.

articles.title_orig: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.title_zh: ABC News quietly suspended staffers behind botched story on Trump sons' business dealings
articles.content_orig:
ABC News has sidelined the staffers behind a botched report about alleged investments tied to President Donald Trump’s children. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto)
ABC News quietly suspended staffers involved in the botched story last month suggesting impropriety in the Trump sons' business dealings, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
The Disney-owned network stirred controversy with its report headlined, "Trump sons' investments have won billions in Pentagon contracts since his election," alleging that Anduril, the company investing in a new Baltimore shipyard, had ties to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump through 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm. The report claimed the firm had a "major stake" in Anduril, which was ultimately false.
ABC News raised eyebrows when it deleted the report without explanation after the story was called out on social media, then quietly republished a revised version of the report with an editor's note acknowledging the error.
GOP SENATOR CALLS FOR FCC PROBE OF ABC NEWS OVER TRUMP SONS-ANDURIL 'POLITICAL HIT JOB'
1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. serves as a partner, has considered legal action against ABC News. (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)
The ordeal resulted in an internal probe to determine what went wrong. While two staffers behind the botched story were reprimanded and rumors they will be terminated swirl, an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "No one's employment status has changed."
ABC News declined further comment.
The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported that the two staffers were on "paid leave."
ABC News' original story wrote, "1789 Capital — a venture capital firm that lists Donald Trump Jr. as one of six partners along with three founders — claimed a major stake in Anduril in June 2025 from a $2.5 billion investment into the company."
"Since that investment, Anduril has been awarded 135 other contracts with the U.S. government and to date has received around $1.8 billion from those agreements, according to active defense contracts posted to SAM.gov , the official system for government contracting," the story continued. "The company is one of the largest manufacturers to receive an investment from Donald Trump Jr. and his brother Eric Trump, but they are not the only one."
ABC NEWS QUIETLY REPUBLISHES GUTTED VERSION OF STORY ON TRUMP SONS IT HAD DELETED WITHOUT EXPLANATION
President Donald Trump and his son, Trump Organization Executive Vice President Eric Trump. (Brendan Moran/Sportsfile via Getty Images)
Alexa Henning, a spokesperson for 1789 Capital and a former chief of staff to the director of national intelligence, took to social media, insisting the company does not have a "major stake" in Anduril and blasting the "biased hit piece."
"Here's a small lesson, that I also explained to ABC, the ‘reporter’ who is a complete idiot conflated raising funds with investment by 1789. Those are two separate actions," Henning reacted at the time .
"Meaning the ‘investments’ mentioned were actually the total number raised for a funding round, that MANY companies contribute to," Henning continued. "Another thing that the reporter buried the lead on was that many of these companies have gotten government contracts during Biden AND Trump, which completely negates the assertion by ABC that Don Jr and Eric Trump are doing anything wrong."
VENTURE CAPITAL FIRM TIED TO DONALD TRUMP JR WEIGHS LEGAL ACTION AGAINST ABC NEWS OVER BOTCHED REPORT
ABC News then sparked confusion among critics when it deleted the entire story, only to republish an overhauled version of the story days later with the new headline reading, "New shipyard announced amid earlier Democratic concerns about potential conflicts of interest" while stressing to readers that Trump Jr. "is not involved in investment decisions."
"CORRECTION: A version of this story published on Oct. 7 contained errors in the description of certain company investments, government contracts and event chronologies," the editor's note read at the top of the article. "After subsequent reporting, this version contains corrected information and additional context regarding some of those investments, contracts and events."
Henning has said that nobody from ABC News asked 1789 for comment prior to the initial story being published and that an ABC News journalist "vigorously defended" the report before it was suddenly deleted. She also previously said the company was considering legal action against the Disney-owned news organization.
"This should be a cautionary tale for any other reporters who continue to traffic in this false narrative," Henning told Fox News Digital on Wednesday when asked if a lawsuit is still being considered.

articles.title_zh: Shelly’s new smart valve shuts off your home’s water before a leak becomes a flood
articles.content_orig:
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
The Neo Smart Water Valve works with Shelly’s sensors to stop a leak in about 12 seconds.﻿
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
After releasing a $28 leak sensor earlier this year that conveniently runs off a battery for two years, Shelly is announcing an accompanying smart valve you can install on your home’s main water line to automatically turn off the flow when one of those sensors detects a problem. The Shelly Neo Smart Water Valve is available now through the company’s online store for $499.99, plus the cost of installation if you don’t trust your plumbing skills. It’s not a cheap solution, but it’s cheaper than the fallout of a leak turning into a disaster.
The Neo Smart Water Valve is designed to be installed on a standard US 1-inch thread connection (the company plans to launch additional size options next year) and is made from brass so it’s safe to use on plumbing carrying drinking water. It has an IPX7 waterproof rating so the valve will keep working if flooding means it ends up submerged. However, the valve lacks a battery of its own and requires a connection to a power source through an included USB adapter cable. Connecting it to a waterproof power bank instead of an outlet may be the best approach to ensure it still works during a power outage.
The smart valve connects to other devices over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and is designed to integrate into existing smart home setups using webhooks, MQTT , or scripting for advanced users. In addition to shutting off the flow of water into your home in about 12 seconds, the valve also features an ultrasonic measurement system that tracks pressure, flow rate, your home’s consumption, and even the temperature of the water. Through the Shelly app, you can monitor all of that data in order to spot unusual usage patterns that could indicate a wasteful leak, or ensure the pressure doesn’t get high enough to damage pipes or appliances.

Diehard GameCube fans can connect the controller to their original console, or use it with the Switch.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad , 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons.
The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices.
8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies , the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers.
The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.
